From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@finedge.com>, Akshay Rao <akshay@vaultbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Thanks — follow up on yesterday's demo and networking questions

Hi Alice — great to meet you yesterday. Looping Akshay in.

Short answers up front:
- Control plane connectivity: For our Private/VPC offering we can operate in two modes: 1) Persistent control-plane connectivity (standard) where the control plane communicates with customer VPC for orchestration and metrics; 2) An alternative 'queued-control' pattern for highly restricted networks where the customer provides an outbound-only egress proxy that polls for a small set of control messages. The latter is not fully air-gapped but avoids inbound openings. Fully air-gapped on-prem (no outbound) requires an on-prem control-plane package — we provide a signed bundle and documented sync windows.

- Scorecard: attached is a preliminary Redwood vs hyperscaler scorecard (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-scorecard.xlsx) with measured p50/p90 from our internal benchmarks and the differences in KV cache persistence. Short takeaways: Redwood maintains KV cache between process restarts for most quantized runtimes; hyperscaler endpoints currently do not expose cache controls and rely on request-level warm starts.

- Proposed 72-hour test plan (high level):
  1) Day 0: Baseline — 1k-token p90 latency per model variant from VaultBank office network to primary region (collect 200 samples).
  2) Day 1: Failover — simulate region outage, measure routing to fallback region and to Dedicated pool (collect 200 samples).
  3) Day 2: Control-plane fallthrough / outbound-only test — use egress proxy to validate queued-control path; verify cache warmstarts and key eviction behavior.

Next steps:
- Akshay, can you share the spare test VLAN and firewall egress rules (IP ranges) so we can pre-seed rules on our side?
- Marissa, can you run the scorecard through infra engineering review and add any requested metrics to the spreadsheet?

I'll upload the network diagram and POAM to the Drive link and attach the scorecard here.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-scorecard.xlsx, network-diff-diagram.png

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: VaultBank POC — scoring rubric + ask list

Marissa / Ben,

Following the external thread, I sketched a pragmatic scoring rubric and an ordered ask list for infra to validate the POC. We should keep this tight — VaultBank wants a decision window next week.

Scorecard (0–3 per category, target >= 18 to recommend Redwood Dedicated):
- Latency (p90, 1k tokens): 0–3
- Failover success (automated reroute within 90s): 0–3
- Cache persistence (KV survive restart, yes/no -> score 0/3): 0–3
- Connectivity modes (fully air-gapped = 0 unless on-prem package; outbound-only queue = 2): 0–3
- Security evidence (SOC2, KMS, audit logs): 0–3
- Cost delta vs hyperscaler (expected token cost %): 0–3

Ask list (ordered):
1) Ben: can you validate the signed on-prem bundle procedure and estimated lead time? Include support SLA for offline installs.
2) Marissa: finalize the scorecard in the spreadsheet and add fields for test artifacts + raw latency traces.
3) Engineering: give a short runbook for the egress-proxy pattern (sample curl-based poll cadence and message sizes).

I'll send the external POC test plan + calendar invite once we have Akshay's test VLAN info.

Cheers,
Soojin
